activeMilestone.exitCondition: All scenarios complete through endings with readable rendering, responsive choices, sustained audio, save/load resume, and measured long-run stability without unsupported stops

lastCompletedBoundary.summary: Release Chrome resumed the validated save and returned to the exact title target after 174.85 seconds with 135 Presents, 10 completed pointer actions, and 5 audio playbacks; no unsupported endpoint, WebGL error, pending host work, lease leak, or source mutation was observed, and the persisted 95,058-byte save remained hash-identical

currentForwardStop.reason: The release forward run returned to the exact title target and stopped with outcome checkpoint-complete after 135 Presents; the final frame independently matched the bounded title color and dark-region probes, while source immutability, zero pending host work, an inactive profile lease, and unchanged save bytes were preserved

nextDevelopmentGoal: Raise actual Chrome play responsiveness through the Rust-authoritative performance execution island and a bounded traced x86 hot path while retaining v86 fallback, then resume additional routes and long-run acceptance

supportedSubsystems.summary: PE32 loading, JIT-enabled x86 execution and the performance island share one Rust-owned GuestMemory arena with checked mapping and write receipts; process/thread scheduling, callbacks and generic forward capture remain active, while normal/debug v86 retain the separate copying mirror and differential oracle

Logical window, message queue, timers, focus/cursor state, keyboard scan, primary down/up dispatch, and native double-click generation are active; the validated save/load continuation accepted input through the first route ending and exact title return

GDI/GDI+ reached paths and bounded D3D9 fixed-function scenes publish through WebGL2; the ending run produced 135 Presents and returned to the exact title color and dark-region signature with WebGL error zero

Immutable source reads and a title-local SQLite overlay remain separated; the latest 95,058-byte Q.Save stayed hash-identical through the ending run with the lease inactive afterward, while the executable and source assets remained unchanged

Reached DirectSound streaming buffers support concurrent non-overlapping partial and wrapping Lock/Unlock, captured notification waits, cursor/status/control, and Play/Stop through generation-safe Chrome Web Audio transport; five non-zero playbacks occurred in the ending run and sustained audio spans the accepted route

importantNonClaims: Only the first default route ending is accepted; alternate choices, alternate routes, all-scenario completion, and long-run acceptance are not yet claimed

The accepted checkpoint is .work-only and retains one 95,058-byte Q.Save with SHA-256 0cd7c853e9c4afd032e9f1235c2a9bb065d6b5a15cb35fc57c87921a991306ec; the ending run hydrated it unchanged and did not overwrite it
The measured route live set is bounded to 480 MiB; later-route peak memory and long-run reclamation are not yet accepted
Primary audio spans the representative flow, but format breadth, suspend/resume behavior, and long-run streaming stability are not yet accepted

Performance mode retains JIT across data mapping changes, selectively rearms dirty-page TLB entries, and delivers independent live host completions without historical replay serialization (two measured transitions improved from 4.42s/3.33s to 1.60s/0.54s). Fused x87 memory operations, exact binary32 widening, guarded native 53-bit arithmetic and batched memory-journal allocation further reduced a CPU-heavy transition from 3.76-4.11s to 2.70-2.83s in Chrome (two runs per variant). Startup through 12 inputs improved from 52.17-53.30s to 50.10-50.26s at 279-287M guest instructions/sec, with zero observed audio underruns but 83ms maximum slices. Independent normal-engine differential checks cover rounding, precision, special values and exponent boundaries; memory rollback retains original bytes and ordering. The normal/debug v86 artifact is unchanged. Whole-run Presents/sec is not steady-play FPS, and 60 FPS-class response remains unaccepted

The direct-memory performance island removes CPU/GuestMemory page copies while preserving Rust frame ownership, zero-initialization, checked protection and transactional rollback. Chrome 152.0.7977.83 startup/12-input runs used 539MB of Wasm memory versus 660MB with the previous MMX island; measured TS writeback synchronization fell from 1.11-1.18s to about 64ms, but wall time remained 50.4-51.7s and maximum slices reached 70-116ms across startup/load checks. Normal/debug keep their unchanged artifact and diagnostic heap fills. These results establish memory/copy reduction, not 60 FPS or a broad speedup

The direct-memory isolated load check hydrated the accepted 95,058-byte save, consumed 20 pointer actions and preserved its hash, source files and inactive lease with no pending work. Its final frame was black and sustained audio underruns remained; a real manual mouse/Enter check also delivered trusted input but did not establish subsequent visual progress. A separate automated-frame-probe fix avoids retaining a black transition sample forever; manual performance mode still omits that probe. Further execution, scheduling and audio investigation is required before accepting playable load continuation or sustained responsiveness
Historical per-API capability profiles are frozen and are not the active development queue
